[[Bosnia and Herzegovina]] sent athletes to the [[Summer Olympic Games]] under its own flag for the first time in [[1992 Summer Olympics|1992]]. Bosnian athletes competed under the Yugoslav flag (see [[Yugoslavia at the Olympics]]) until the [[Breakup of Yugoslavia|breakup of that country]]. Along with [[Andorra at the Olympics|Andorra]], [[Malta at the Olympics|Malta]], and [[Monaco at the Olympics|Monaco]], Bosnia and Herzegovina is one of four current European participants that have never won an Olympic medal.

The [[Olympic Committee of Bosnia and Herzegovina]] was formed in 1992 and recognized in 1993.

== Pre-1992 Yugoslavian medalists from Bosnia-Herzegovina ==
Bosnian-Herzegovinian athletes have won medals on many occasions in different sports as part of teams and one as individual competitors (boxing) representing [[Yugoslavia at the Olympics|Yugoslavia]].<ref name=OKBiH>{{cite web |publisher=Olympic Committee of Bosnia and Herzegovina |title=PARTICIPATION OF THE BH. ATHLETES IN ASSERTION OF THE OLYMPIC MOVEMENT |url=http://www.okbih.ba/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=152&Itemid=12&lang=en |author=Besalet Kazazovic |language=en, bs |access-date=12 November 2013 |archive-date=1 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150201191436/http://www.okbih.ba/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=152&Itemid=12&lang=en |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=Varaja>{{cite web|last=Sports-Reference.com|title=Žarko Varajić Biography and Olympic Results {{!}} Olympics at Sports-Reference.com|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/va/zarko-varajic-1.html|publisher=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=7 August 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102235704/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/va/zarko-varajic-1.html|archive-date=2 November 2012|df=dmy-all}}</ref>
